extras.descricao_original: About MEXT MEXT Ministerial Team List of Senior Officials Organization MEXT Logo Address of MEXT Museum of MEXT Related Sites Policy Policy Index Budget National Councils Education Science and Technology Sports Culture Report＆Statistics White Paper Statistics Report Related Sites First Meeting of the Japan-Ukraine Joint Commission on Education, Science and Technology Cooperation Monday, July 29, 2024 Education, Science and Technology, Academia, Culture and Arts, Sport, International On July 29, MEXT Minister MORIYAMA Masahito attended the first meeting of the Japan-Ukraine Joint Commission on Education, Science and Technology Cooperation also attended by Ukraine’s Minister of Education and Science, Oksen Lisovyi. The heads exchanged views on areas in need of advancing collaboration in the fields of education, science, and technology. A Joint Summary was signed (as attached). During the meeting, Minister Moriyama highlighted invitations of Ukrainian high school students, university students and researchers to Japan, donations of Japanese picture books and support for their publication, cooperation in international joint research, and requested Ukraine’s cooperation in these efforts. The Joint Commission on Japan-Ukraine Education, Science and Technology Cooperation was established on occasion of the Japan-Ukraine Conference on Promotion of Economic Reconstruction was held in Tokyo this February. The first bilateral Joint Commission was held in Kyiv, Ukraine, and was co-chaired by Minister Moriyama. The MEXT Minister also met with Ukraine’s Acting Minister of Culture and Information Policy, Rostyslav Karandieiev, and exchanged views on cultural facilities, restoration of cultural properties and cultural exchange between the two countries. Minister Moriyama conveyed his support for the protection of Ukraine's cultural heritage and in holding performances in Japan. Based on the results of this these meetings, MEXT will work on the “MEXT Support Package for Ukraine” to contribute to Ukraine in areas under MEXT's jurisdiction. titulo: Cooperation with the U.S. Department of Energy on Improving Proliferation Resistance in a Research Reactor
descricao: About MEXT MEXT Ministerial Team List of Senior Officials Organization MEXT Logo Address of MEXT Museum of MEXT Related Sites Policy Policy Index Budget National Councils Education Science and Technology Sports Culture Report＆Statistics White Paper Statistics Report Related Sites Cooperation with the U.S. Department of Energy on Improving Proliferation Resistance in a Research Reactor The Pro-X (Proliferation Resistance Optimization) program is a DOE/NNSA effort, launched in 2019, to incorporate proliferation resistance concepts beginning in the design phase of research reactors. On April 25, Mr. Hiroshi Masuko, Deputy Minister of MEXT, and Ms. Jill Hruby, Administrator of the NNSA, agreed to proceed with Pro-X activities through the cooperation between Japan and the United States. As part of this cooperation, they agreed to proceed with efforts in the design stage of the new research reactor at the Monju site, which is led by the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA) and expected to be widely used for education, training, and research. They also agreed to advance cooperation to increase the proliferation resistance of research reactors in emerging nuclear power countries including the Asian region. MEXT will promote this initiative in order to improve nuclear nonproliferation and nuclear security, which is a common goal of both countries. Nuclear Energy Division, Research and Development Bureau genshi@mext.go.jp International Nuclear and Fusion Energy Affairs Division, Research
